Imperial Censor Investigators.name: Imperial Censor Investigators
Imperial Censor Investigators.text:
The position of the Imperial Censors was established by the first Shu Emperor, Jiao Deng Shu (wise male human emperor). A bureaucrat before ascending to the throne, Shu understood the importance of oversight. Empires function only through complex systems that require the work of countless clerks and ministers, all of whom could fall prey to corruption or favoritism by the various powerbrokers which constitute the aristocracy. To ensure a long and peaceful dynasty, the emperor emboldened the ranks of the Imperial Censors, granting them the power to enforce the virtues of the great sages of the past, demanding them to hold all imperial subjects—including the emperor—to be accountable for their actions.

It was Yixing’s fall into illiteracy and superstition which upended centuries of precedent, that would be the catalyst for the formation and downfall of the Imperial Censors. It would be the censors who were tasked with restoring justice to the land, order to the courts, truth to the archives, and a taxing rebirth to bureaucratic institutions across the whole of Tian Xia. It was in these long throes of reconstruction and collapse that the first documented cases of corruption emerged in the ranks of the Imperial Censors. With the bureaucracy in shambles and their order spread thin, new censors brought forth new ideas, for good or ill; while old censors skirted the line between traditionalists and belligerents. For every prodigy who scored at the highest on the Imperial Examinations there would be another censor who received a posting due to favoritism in the courts. The censors themselves questioned the limits of their authority, as though their task was for the good of the people, only the Shu emperor could hold them accountable. While some would reopen old cases to challenge aristocrats who thought themselves above the law, others would pursue baseless claims to manipulate the courts or diminish rivals to their clans. Tales of virtuous censors fighting for the common people became popular themes in Shu operas, though the depth of any real internal conflict remained wilfully obscured by censors on either side.

During the later reign of the despotic Lung Wa Empire, censors became synonymous with corruption serving, as enforcers of vindictive rulers and justifying their every atrocity with cherry picked rhetoric from far more noble regimes. Devoid of morality and their station diminished, many corrupt censors would die at the hands of assassins, rivals, or the people they claimed to protect. In this time, an honest censor was rarer than summer snow, but the legend of their struggles for justice only grew stronger in the stories of folklorists and novelists. In the present day, without a single emperor or unified empire, the Imperial Censors are a relic of the past. While their methods are still taught and used by modern investigators, those who would claim themselves an Imperial Censor lack the authority and backing of imperial power. However, the censors' deep knowledge of academic minutia and imperial regulations remains invaluable to those who inherit this legal tradition, and those who pursue such scholarship are well-valued in the bureaucracies of the Successor States. Without a single emperor to be beholden to, few can be sure if this new generation of Imperial Censors will wield their courtly graces for the good of all nations, or if they will engage in the same malpractice which tarnished their order to its current state.

Qi Shaper.name: Qi Shaper
Qi Shaper.text:
• Uncommon

Chu Ye was once the center of study for qi, the life essence that flows through all creatures and plants. Originally practitioners focused on medical treatments, but powerful martial artists also emerged who sought to extract qi from the most dangerous place of all: their own spirit. These martial qi shapers developed techniques to extract the spirit itself through distinct points of the body, exuding the energy in the process. The most common qi shape being a powerful blow, which exacts a toll on the body and spirit alike. Though qi shaping is similar to other methods of qi manipulation, shapers bend qi in ways that other practitioners of qi have long considered at best to be unorthodox and all too often reckless, even if its methods may prove fruitful to the shapers

NEW TRAIT Qi-Shape: A qi-shape action is a special action that requires that you have at least 1 Focus Point remaining in your Focus Pool. You must spend 1 Focus Point when you use the Energize entry for a qi-shape action, and doing so modifies the action’s properties as described in its entry. You cannot use more than one qi-shape action per turn. When you gain a new qi-shape action, you increase your Focus Pool by 1 point.

Qi To Life: Qi is closely connected to life and is many faceted in how it harbors connections. There are many different ways to utilize qi, often with unique goals between those which seek to access the essence of life. The shapers wield qi in a dangerous way, using their own life essence at a cost for greater power. As this use of qi causes great risk to their own spirit, others within the study of these life essences may find shapers reckless practicioners.

Tsukumogami Poppets

Tsukumogami begin their lives as unharvested materials, soaking up energy from their natural surroundings. Then, laborers enrich these materials with intentionality, each purposeful movement transforming trees into wood, soil into clay, and rock into metal. Crafters further the process, pouring their mental energies and creativity into elevating the resources from mere raw materials into finished products. These dormant tsukumogami continue gathering energies from their new home and family, finally awakening after a hundred years of love and care.

Though shaped by love and respect, tsukumogami are alien to many, often inspiring fright in others; few humanoids are prepared for the monstrous, flapping mouths and hopping locomotions many tsukumogami use to get around. Some tsukumogami even delight in their bizarre natures and aptitude at terror, in the same way that some children giggle when they unnerve an adult. Most of them aren’t malicious; they’re just playing a game that only they know the rules to. Other tsukumogami poppets recognize their effects on humanoids and take pains to be as unobtrusive as possible, disappearing into their environments and helping behind the scenes.

Both kinds of tsukumogami can become excellent adventurers. The former wield fear as a weapon, making them intimidating combatants, capable of demoralizing and terrorizing their foes. The latter excel at lending helpful spells to their allies and performing investigations, especially ones involving other tools or the Lore skill they gained as part of their heritage.

Kaiju Caller.name: Kaiju Caller
Kaiju Caller.text:
• Rare

In the wake of the colossal calamities known as kaiju, only the wisdom of the Kaiju Callers allows civilization to endure. These learned scholars and survivalists study every facet of the titanic beings in search of hidden truths, sifting through folklore and mythic parables, the hearsay of survivors and the records of sundered kingdoms. They scrutinize each and every detail to determine patterns in behavior, diets, desires, and dangers. From this insight, innocent lives can be saved and titanic beasts may be contended with; less as natural disasters and more as wayward beasts.

Kaiju Callers defend themselves and others against the great monsters of the world. To fulfill their duty they master rituals anchored in ever-changing songs and protective dances, to beckon and rebuke as needs have it. To survive their duties, they must master tactics and cunning enough to remain beneath the notice of the kaiju while mitigating the most harm possible. At their mightiest, if the bluster of the Valash Raj can be believed, some Kaiju Callers can even invoke their knowledge of kaiju to wield their power, if only for an instance.

Joseongyin Shrinekeeper.name: Joseongyin Shrinekeeper
Joseongyin Shrinekeeper.text:
• Uncommon

To the uninitiated, the northeastern coast of Hwanggot pales in comparison to the jewels of Haseong and Maecho. Ask any studied Tian-Hwan bureaucrat and they would struggle to think of a standout among the villages that dot the floodplains. However, ask any rural dweller of those same villages and they will all agree one place stands above the rest: Yaju, a small city tucked just south of Hwanggot's easternmost peninsula. At first glance, Yaju is a deceptively quiet city whose primary point of interest is a red-bean pastry resembling two stacked pancakes. Only those who take the time to delve deeper will find Yaju is less a city and more a living historical record, one that exists as an open secret; overlooked in the long history of conflict in Tian Xia. This record is housed in a cylindrical building called the Joyaga which sits innocuously in a field by Yaju’s town center. Locals delight in asking the rare visitor to their city what they think it might be (“an observatory?” “a watchtower?”) and watching their shock as seemingly thousands of sparrows descend on the centuries-old aviary every sunset, guided there by joseongyin (jo- suhng-een), lantern-bearing devotees of Phi Deva who tend to this flock. Among the dedicated lantern-bearer servants of Phi Deva, only the most skilled train to become shrinekeepers and obtain the position of joseongyin. These members consider themselves both as birds within the flock and the flock itself, seeking to find the same inter-connectivity that defines the Thousand- Souled Chorus on the mortal plane.

Nagajor Monsoon Expert.name: Nagajor Monsoon Expert
Nagajor Monsoon Expert.text:
• Uncommon

With Nagajor being situated on wetlands and beset by seasonal downpours, the risk of flooding is ever present. Rivers, once the lifeblood of commerce and agriculture become dangerous, even fatal, if one misreads the coming storm. To combat the elements and safeguard its residents, Nagajor has a faction of experts capable of preserving infrastructure and rescuing citizens under threat of a monsoon’s deluge. Individuals who claim training as a Nagajor’s monsoon experts are often viewed with a status that mirrors their potential merit, as their role in the nation serves as a reminder that those willing to risk their lives for the good of their countrymen are to be admired.

These monsoon experts are trained to navigate the rivers, floodwaters and storm surges as easily as the streets of their communities. They can wade through the strongest currents, build temporary dams out of scraps in a pinch, and even redirect water flow to reduce river swelling. Prior to the monsoon season, they keep watch of the river ways and monitor rainfall, preparing distributaries to move water away from the main rivers where the extra water can be used for irrigation.

While flooding is all but guaranteed during monsoon season, it remains a risk all year round. As such, Nagajor monsoon experts are always busy, whether it be a flood, a mudslide, pestilence, or some other disaster tangential to the monsoon itself. Many monsoon experts often find themselves in the role of guides for travelers in Nagajor, as this grants them further social accolades and allows them to prevent diplomatic incidents should nature reveal how dangerous it truly is.

Minatan Warrior Dedication.name: Minatan Warrior Dedication
Minatan Warrior Dedication.text:
• Uncommon

Just as Minata has a wide variety of linguistic communities among its islands, it has a range of names for its national martial arts: dōg, sōsen, kalis, and many more. Although each Minatan culture has its own preference for what to call the martial art, the term Minatan Martial Arts has arisen as a popular way to avoid favoring any group, with practitioners referred to as “Minatan warriors,” or simply “warriors.” Despite the variety in names, the foundational techniques remain much the same throughout the islands.

The center of Minatan Martial Arts is practical fighting, using the same core moves with a variety of weapons to maximize training value. While a pair of kalis are the ideal weapon for Minatan warriors, not everyone has access to swords at all times. Thus, the same strikes and blocks also apply to paired rattan stick fighting, machetes, hand-to- hand, and more. Drilling these moves prepares Minatan warriors to fight effectively with whatever they have available. And, while some might think of twin rattan clubs as beginner weapons incapable of doing much harm, the swift power of them when wielded by a Minatan warrior demonstrates the error of that thinking. Strikes and blocks in Minatan Martial Arts drills follow quick, arcing patterns, allowing warriors to practice at full speed, building the muscle memory needed to deliver punishing slashes and block incoming attacks by reflex alone.

Minatan Martial Arts: The potency of Minatan Martial Arts was put to the test when the Teikoku Shogunate sailed their fleet to conquer the archipelago of a hundred nations. As a land with dozens of kings, Minata had no hope of creating a united front to put up a defense. That didn’t matter. Minata’s coral reefs shredded the invaders’ ships, and where the samurai were able to fight, they didn’t stand a chance. The ferocity of the Minatan warriors and the lightning speed of their attacks tore the samurai to shreds. The vicious attacks of Minatan Martial Arts won the day over and over, until the Teikoku Shogunate fled, leaving the Wandering Isles independent.

Three-Finger Fist Dedication.name: Three-Finger Fist Dedication
Three-Finger Fist Dedication.text:
The style itself concentrates on defense and disrupting the opponent's attacks. Though sai are often thought of as stabbing weapons, their true purpose is to parry incoming blows and deliver punishing bludgeoning ripostes. The Three-Finger Fist style recognizes two grips and trains its martial artists to transition between them with speed and power. The open hand grip faces all three prongs to the opponent, staying ready to catch opponents’ weapons, crush their wrists, or thrust at the collarbone. The iron forearm grip places the sai alongside the outside of the wielder’s forearm, allowing traditional unarmed blocks to turn aside blades, as well as facilitating jabs that channel their force through the thin handle. The result is a style that excels at disrupting and disarming foes.

Starlit Sentinel.name: Starlit Sentinel
Starlit Sentinel.text:
While the Starlit Sentinels are the most popular and famous team of magical sentinels out to protect Golarion, they are not the only ones. Different sources of magic and influence have taken inspiration from the 12 constellations to give people that they deem worthy of powers to form teams, or work solo, to protect and defend the people and places around them. For example, Darling Dame Kirakira (Silly female aiuvarin protector) is a solo sentinel with the power of her village’s ancestors. She has become something of a local celebrity, though the villagers have no idea that this sentinel is Ramiko Tazigari (Gentle female aiuvarin shrine keeper), who smiles softly when they leave offerings to the ancestors that guide Darling Dame Kirakira. There is also the Celestial Wildcourt, a group of heroes empowered by the nature spirits that protect the environment wherever they go from those who would seek to destroy or exploit it.

These groups vary in size and power across Tian Xia and the rest of Golarion. The source of their powers are defined by the particular flavor a group has, allowing for an arcane trait to instead be divine, or occult, or primal depending on the theming of the sentinel.

Intro.name: Intro
Intro.text:
Foreward

Tian Xia is a vast and expansive region that spans many countries and cultures in its representation, which is what made this Team+ venture a special venture. The first step to ensuring that we made a fair and honest effort to be faithful and easily integrated to the already established setting in Golarion meant we had to find the right team for the job. We couldn’t ask for a better team of people for this book, many of which authored content for the Tian Xia setting books by Paizo. Not only is this the largest team of authors for a Team+ to date, it is also our largest book so far. We believe this book is a step for us to approach content that finds its roots in real life culture in an appropriate way, and we hope that is the first of many in which we take this approach to production. We believe the work will speak for itself. We hope you think so too.

Tian Xia+

Opportunity and danger abound in Tian Xia, and people rise to meet both in ways as diverse as the land itself. From the horse lords of Hongal riding across vast steppes to disaster responders in Nagajor wading through monsoon floods, there are many paths to becoming heroes. Some start their journey through circumstance, such as those who become host to a kami or whose homeland faces rampaging kaiju, while others discover their calling through training, whether as a martial artist, a starlit sentinel, a devoted shrinekeeper, or a dragon’s emissary.

Minatan Dancer.name: Minatan Dancer
Minatan Dancer.text:
• Uncommon

Though each of the wandering isles are unique in their traditions, all Minatans enjoy a common cultural touchstone in the syncretic blend of dance and martials arts performed by martial dancers. As a performance art it is popular among monks and athletes, as well as historians who use the dance to display the epic tales of ancient heroes. While flashing blades are well- established crowd pleasers, other martial dancers wield coconuts as instruments and armor; performing the maglalatik in grand pugilistic displays. Whatever their style, martial dancers are some of the most graceful warriors and storied performers one could ever have the privilege of watching. Those who venture beyond the isles of Minata carry the legacy of their homes with them, entrancing audiences as readily as they outmaneuver their enemies.

Tang Mai Conductor.name: Tang Mai Conductor
Tang Mai Conductor.text:
• Uncommon

The Tang Mai conductor is both a musician and a leader. They lead orchestras and weave magic into their songs. Each note played draws from the abundant magics of the Sikhyeu Forest.

There is no formalized university to become a Tang Mai conductor, as calling upon spirits to produce music is a deeply personal connection to both music and the spirits themselves. Anyone may learn the rules of musical composition, but to become a true conductor, one must apprentice under a master. These masters form an unbroken line of scholars, each with their own songs, their own way to draw from the world and create stories through music, carrying on a legacy that transcends recorded history. Apprentices first prove their potential as members of an orchestra, specializing in one of the many instruments available and learning the fullness of its nuances. Only once a deeper knowledge of music is obtained can one dare consider themselves worthy of being a conductor.

Though their initiation rites are esoteric to most, Tang Mai conductors are well known across Tian Xia, sharing their songs and learning the stories of the lands they travel through. They are viewed by most as nomadic, traveling from place to place at the whims of inspiration. They often play at festivals, markets, restaurants, but are just as likely to be found performing as buskers on the street. As a conductor gains renown, they are sought after by nobles, religious institutions, and even the occasional warlord. Conductors with these more permanent postings are viewed as shows of luxury and legacy, as only hosts capable of inspiring through deeds and merit can obtain the blessings a Tang Mai conductor provides.

Conducting Orchestrations: Tang Mai orchestrations are music pieces that can be prepared during exploration or downtime. Orchestrations take an hour to prepare, as you spend time orchestrating the performance with your spirit performers and choosing an orchestration you know to prepare. After you complete your preparation, you can spend a single action that has the concentrate trait to summon a group of spirit performers in a 20-foot burst within 30 feet of you. These spirit performers grant the effects of your orchestration to creatures within the area for 1 minute.

An orchestration requires a Performance check to prepare, which you do during your hour of preparation. If you have the required proficiency rank, you can attempt checks against a higher DC to create additional effects. A creature cannot be affected by more than one orchestration at a time and must choose which effect to keep if they would gain the effects of another.

Valash Summoners

The summoner traditions of the Valashmai Jungle are like many things in the Valash Raj, a usurpation of the Valashai’s legacy as slavers and a syncretic recontextualization of the many disparate parts the otherworldly conquerors brought to these lands. Many summoned Eidolons are invoked at unparalleled sizes and capable of widespread destructive might, akin to the region’s many kaiju. Others instead take on primeval, primordial forms, drawing on the geomantic powers of the Valashai, unsullied by their hubristic peaks of excess. Regardless what shape an Eidolon is rendered into, the summoners of Valash Raj look upon their grand works as they do everything the Valashai once held: as grand achievements of power which must be wielded responsibly, lest a grim legacy of monsters repeat itself again.

Soulforger Mythic Expansion.text:
Across Tian Xia, groups of like minded Soulforgers have come together to collaboratively train in pursuit of their soul paths. Community, collective dedication in these pursuits further empower the soulforgers. Color coordinated outfits and a penchant for the dramatic has led to public opinion calling them the “Super Soul Warriors”, much to their chagrin. The activities of these larger collectives easily garner the attention from various powers—deities, planar beings, and extraplanar entities. That these soulforgers make a habit of seeking out lost relics, magical crystals, and ancient mystic beasts to supplement their mythic abilities make even the heavens wary.

Mythic Soulforgers

Mythic Soulforgers choose from among any mythic calling. You gain the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.SNjmjFw30KQxIP4A]{Rewrite Fate} mythic free action, but can only use this when your armament’s essence form is manifested. You regain a Mythic Point when critically succeeding at a Strike with your soulforged weapon or when you are critically hit with a Strike while wearing your soulforged armor or wielding your soulforged shield in essence form. You can only regain a Mythic Point this way once per day.

Planar Burst (Mythic) Weapon only. When you manifest the essence form, choose one damage type: acid, cold, electricity, fire, sonic, vitality, or void. You deal 1d6 additional damage of this type with your weapon. When you successfully Strike with a soul armament weapon, you can spend 1 Mythic point to project a 15-foot cone using a space within reach of your weapon that the target occupies as the first square of the cone. This deals 1d4 damage per two levels you possess of the chosen damage type. You can spend additional Mythic Points to double the length of the cone and also increase the damage die by one step. Corruption Flaw You take 1d6 damage of the chosen type each time you deal damage with a weapon or unarmed attack. This damage bypasses any resistances or immunities you have, but still triggers any weaknesses.

Soul Survivor (Mythic) Armor or shield only. Gain temporary hit points equal to twice your level that last until the essence effect ends. If you would be reduced to 0 Hit Points or die, you can choose to spend a Mythic Point as a free action to break your soulforged armament armor or shield, to immediately regain half your Hit Points, and fall prone. Corruption Flaw You become drained 2.

Soulbond Sculptor (Mythic) When you manifest the essence form of your soul armament, spend 1 Mythic Point to gain the effects of a property rune of your level or lower that your soul armament does not already have. This property rune does not count towards the limit of property runes for your weapon. Corruption Flaw You lose the benefits of one of your armament’s property runes at random.

Selective Resilience (Mythic) Armor or shield only. Choose a damage type: bludgeoning, piercing, slashing, or spirit. You gain resistance equal to your level against the chosen type. Body of the Kami.text:
• Rare

Kami are spirits tied to objects, creatures, or locations who have a divine mission to protect their vessel. They typically associate with trees or geographical features, though some may bond with objects discarded in the wilderness. All share a goal of protecting the natural world. In rare instances, a kami may bond with a humanoid or other creature associated with the very civilizations whose encroachment kami oppose. This host may be a key ally of nature, a being with a divine destiny that aligns with the goals of the kami, or a victim of possession by a kami which has all but fallen from station. While the kami is aware of their purpose, the host may not be. The kami acts as protector and teacher, ensuring their host is prepared for the part they must play.

Imperial Dragon Emissaries.name: Imperial Dragon Emissaries
Imperial Dragon Emissaries.text:
Imperial dragons meddle in the affairs of Tian Xia’s civilizations more often than their counterparts in other parts of the world, viewing their intercessions upon the nations as demonstrations of proper stewardship or as their innate right within the hierarchy of beings. Their claims of dominion are far from bluster, for the very land itself was formed from the bodies of their ancestors, and Shizuru, the Ruler of Heaven, has granted them a divine mandate to safeguard the continent for humanity.

But even the mightiest of Imperial dragons must know they can’t accomplish everything themselves, especially when humanity must prove its mettle and establish itself as the rightful inheritors of Tian Xia, as Shizuru wishes. Thus these dragons establish networks of trusted advisors and emissaries through whom they exert their influence across the land. Those who obtain the esteem of a dragon may become their emissary, gaining access to their vaults of powerful items and becoming imbued with a portion of their magical powers.

Imperial dragons choose only powerful individuals who have achieved success both as adventurers and in more subtle ways, primarily by mirroring some personal trait that the dragon sees within itself and finds laudable in another. A dragon imposes anathema and edicts on its emissaries when they first gain this archetype. If you perform enough acts that are anathema, you lose the magical abilities that come from your connection to your dragon. The feats and abilities that you lose are determined by the GM, but they likely include any spellcasting or actions that would invoke your dragon’s power. These abilities can be regained only if you repent by conducting an atone ritual.

Imperial Reputation

This section describes five named dragons from Lost Omens: Tian Xia World Guide, one of each imperial dragon type, with the goal of providing as many tools as possible for both player and GMs to shape a detailed story. These selected dragons exemplify many of the typical traits of their type, allowing this information to be applied to another dragon of that type with minimal modification based on the needs of your table.

Use the Reputation System described in GM Core (Chapter 4: Subsystems - Reputation) to track the character’s or party’s relationship with the dragon. Since characters are unlikely to meet a dragon in person early in the game, track instead their activities affecting the dragon’s area of concern. Each dragon exercises domain over a physical region of Tian Xia, but they also have specific interests across all of Tian Xia. When a character impacts either, their actions count as favors if they align with the dragon’s edicts or disservices if they fall under the dragon’s anathemas.

Dragons may reach out to characters as early as when they are Liked but most reserve their approach for when they feel the character can act according to their expectations. However, dragons may still approach characters who are Ignored or have a negative reputation if the characters stumble into one of the dragon’s plots or are in close physical proximity to the dragon and the dragon has a use for them.

The dragon is only willing to lend certain items from their vault or bestow temporary abilities to low level characters and characters with a reputation lower than Liked. Higher level characters and characters with a better reputation become trusted emissaries. They gain access to the dragon’s emissary archetype and may receive items permanently as gifts.

Forest Dragon
Arindham of the Valashmai Jungle

As has happened once before in Kashang, an interloper sought to pilfer that which was best left buried. The poison spread and twisted the land, a toxin born from the slaver Valashai of old; and from this despoiling came Akaran, the kaiju guardian spirit, and a great calamity upon our world. I have received word from Arindham, the Great Guardian, that a similar doom shall now befall us.They claim that the Dark Brood has breached a sealed ruin in which untold monstrosities thought lost to time were imprisoned. And upon their horrid forms, an incurable rot. The Brood, foolish and proud, wield this rot like reckless children, seeking to expand their territory. This circumstance is unacceptable.

Do not be deluded by what your eyes perceive. There is little in the Valashmai Jungle that is natural. All that remains of what nature ordains is held in by Arindham, and they jealously protect that life. For the moment our ambitions align, this rot must be stopped, the damage contained—but none shall escape their wrath once this service is done. Arindham awaits those with mettle enough to reach where the Chenlun Mountains descend to the western bank of the Swamp of the Dark Brood’s river border. They offer powerful boons to any willing to reverse the rot’s effects and enact retribution against the Dark Brood. Send your bravest, send your best, and pray their victories shall win you Arindham’s clemency. Otherwise, make peace with your gods.

-Letter from Otar Sultan to leaders of surrounding nations

Home preserve of natural forest in southwest Valashmai Jungle

Primary Region of Concern Valashmai Jungle

Edicts defend nature against those who would exploit its resources, destroy that which is artificial, oppose the encroachment of civilization, reclaim whatever you can for nature

Anathemas allow the pursuit of perfection to override practicality, create unnatural creatures, diseases, and toxins, harm untouched areas of nature

Other Interests limited use of bioengineering and geoengineering to reverse damage to the jungle

Aridham's Quest

Arindham’s request is two-fold. First, they need adventurers to stop and, if possible, reverse the spread of the rot. Second, they want to make an example of the Dark Brood for their hubris, as well as punish any seeking to take advantage of these events

This quest would fit in well with campaigns set in or around the Valashmai Jungle which involve threats from kaijus, elementals, or plunderers seeking treasure from the ruins of fallen empires now hidden by the jungle’s growth. It could either be another threat that arises in the course of the campaign’s progress or be the origin of the threats that kicked off the campaign, such as the rot displacing other groups or arousing the ire of kaijus. Whatever the cause for the adventure, it need only be present in the jungle and be of note for Arindham to place their claw on the scale of the fortune of the adventurers.

Moderate favors for Arindham are establishing sanctuaries elsewhere in Valashmai Jungle to temporarily relocate animals, plants, and fungi threatened by the rot, defeating the time-lost horrors released from the tomb and preventing them from spreading more rot, as well as bringing in allies who can fight the Dark Brood or counter other threats left over from the Jade Hegemon and the Valashai Empire.

Major favors would be finding a cure for the rot, destroying the leaders of the Dark Brood who unleashed the rot, and expanding areas of natural forest against the invasive, artificial flora and fauna of Valashmai Jungle.

Sea Dragon
Luong Phung of Xidao

All jaws drop at the Convocation of the Grand Council as Mewru’s representatives declare independence from not only Western Xidao but the entire confederacy. The initial shock quickly gives way to disdain against what is frankly more a pirate haven than a true city-state. The crowd jeers and I hear what sounds like the familiar voice of another ambassador, though I hesitate to record a name lest I be mistaken.

Finally—I say that though likely less than half a minute had passed—the High Matriarch motions for order and silence arrives like deafness after an explosion. Mewru’s lead ambassador takes the opportunity to continue her speech, though with a noticeable tremble in her voice. Mewru will be leaving the confederacy to join a new alliance… with Aya- Maru.

Bubbles erupt around the conference as people gasp. Some athamarus and ocean giants faint. I hear a few giggles from people unsure if it is a joke.

“Aya-Maru has revealed its full strength to us,” the lead ambassador continues, her voice now steady but flat and cold as death, “and we wish to be… on the winning side.”

A grey athamaru who has been shadowing the ambassador this whole time floats forward. I’d passed them in the hall, their appearance notable for two reasons: first, I had never seen them before and yet they acted as equals to senior ambassadors, and second, something about their presence gave me chills. Now the reason becomes clear, for their body twists and swells, growing as they polymorph from their disguise into their true form.

Patches of scales missing from the bloated body frame gaping wounds left by harpoons and scavengers. The only color upon the once-vibrant sapphire skin is the dull green of algal overgrowth, a ghastly sight I’ve only previously seen upon the bones of bleached coral. One eye is missing, and the opposite antler broken, marring the face of the young sea dragon that was once the pride of Xidao, yet there is no doubt who floats before us: the undead corpse of Luong Lanh, Luong Phung’s only child.

-Report by junior ambassador Melutharac

Home the roaming Tempest of Xidao

Primary Region of Concern Xidao Gulf

Edicts be fair when making deals, honor deals you make, promote diplomacy over violence, respect sea dragons and the waters they control

Anathemas abuse power to take more than your fair share, aid underworld dragons against sea dragon interests, be the aggressor in a violent conflict, harm the reputation of sea dragons as respected mediators

Other Interests grieving her dead child, seeking vengeance against poachers

Luong Phung's Quest

Peace and cooperation between Xidao’s city-states has been Luong Phung’s life’s work. Seeing it fall apart is almost as significant a loss as the death of her only child. In her grief, she invests her entire being into the destruction of whatever evil lies at the bottom of Aya- Maru.

She reasons that working together to vanquish a common foe may forge a national identity among the disparate city-states of Xidao which will ensure lasting unity. However, Luong Phung is compromised at the moment, grief clouds her judgment and forces her to pour the whole of her being into this pursuit. The loss of her child a second time would leave her inconsolable, and none dare consider what may happen should this occur. The city-states demand the heroes restore her child’s soul to the reanimated body, for the good of all who roam the sea. The city-states provide represenatives with a hoard of treasure to offer her in hopes to calm her tempest, but she is likely to calm it to meet them as Xidao’s chosen representatives.

Aquatic adventures are daunting unless a party is prepared for it, making this quest difficul. Aya-Maru poses a major regional threat with political and religious ramifications. As such, this quest would work best as the major threat of a game with smaller encounters building to a confrontation at the bottom of the trench

Moderate favors for Luong Phung involve diplomacy and espionage: acquiring commitments from city-states to oppose Aya-Maru, determining if Mewru truly wants to align with Aya-Maru or is doing so under duress, regaining Mewru’s allegiance, and learning more about Aya-Maru itself.

Major favors include uniting the city-states of Xidao into a long-term alliance, securing the border of Aya- Maru to prevent incursions into Western and Eastern Xidao, identifying the root cause of the undead threat from Aya-Maru, ending the threat from Aya-Maru, and restoring Luong Phung’s child to life by reuniting soul with body.

Luong Phung's Gifts

Luong Phung may provide the following items to adventurers. Shei Long of Mount Tsukiyo

Two types of people brave the annual sacred pilgrimage known as the Tsukiyo Trek in Zi Ha— supplicants to Shei Long who are desperate for answers only an oracle can provide and adventurers foolishly seeking a challenge and incentivized by the hefty sums offered to prospective bodyguards. Ironically, the latter are often the only ones who make it to the end of the brutal twenty-eight day ascent up Mount Tsukiyo. Frostbite, hypothermia, dehydration, carnivorous plants, and ogres are but some of the arduous obstacles that too many pilgrims overlook. Most who start the trek with high hopes and offerings of goat meat and mung bean cakes turn back within days of facing the freezing precipices of the Kelsang mountains and all that would find them wanting.

Yet every year the masses flock in anticipation of the attempt, for whispers abound that Shei Long grants those who reach the top a sublime insight into how they might achieve their heart’s desires. Those who return are often pensive and silent about what they learned, and gossip always fills the void. It is a different mood than what I recall from glimpses of my past life, when many were jubilant or determined about what lay ahead. I sought to learn the truth from Shei Long herself. The end of the journey was an incredible moment—no leader or member of the Oracular Advisory Council had completed the Trek in two generations, much less one as young as I! The warrior guides who volunteered to accompany me burst into song to express their joy, and I couldn’t help but join my voice to theirs. Then the great sky dragon descended from the sky, her coils parting the frost and fog, and her expression froze our celebration faster than the night wind cools melting snow.

–Personal notes of Tian Zenwyn

The smell of sesame oil, beer, and stale sweat hang in the air. Patrons have no qualms with shouting conversation over both each other and the merry sound of the band tonight, and the resulting cacophony is enough to deafen. It’s a typical scene inside of the Gilded Nghê, a pub nestled in the backstreets of Ngōn Hoa.

Suddenly, a cheer goes up near the entrance, and carousers rush to clear away a table in the center of the pub. A golden-eyed man in intricate silk robes and laden with strings of pearls around his neck and arms and thin chains of gold and jewels leads an equally well-dressed posse. He stands on the table with a bellowing laugh and showers the bartenders in gold, declaring that everyone drinks with him today.

Someone doesn’t join the frenzy as beer and rượu are poured into the glasses patrons already hold. Instead, they slip away from their table and approach the bejeweled man, who sits alone now that his retinue has been swallowed up by the crowd. They bow to him and wait to stand until he gives permission to do so. He gestures to sit beside him, and once they’re settled, I read their mouth’s movements and learn as they tell Supreme Commander Pham Lê Ngọc everything they’ve overheard while attending a banquet held by the People’s Reformation Order the night before.

Geojibom of the Darklands

Beyond the everpresent gloom and the stale air I’m forced to breathe, the worst part of the Darklands is how day and night bleed together into one liminal stretch of time. The last glimmering vestiges of Rahk Lo have long since disappeared behind me, and all that’s left is the murky darkness ahead. Perhaps that’s why it takes me just a little too long to realize that the stalactites along the ceiling are… wrong. These jagged tooth-like structures have been carefully sanded into mockeries of trees. It makes me long for the sunlit world above, with branches reaching for my head rather than towards the faux sky.

This sudden homesickness spurs me to action. Venturing so close to Orv was a mistake. I miss my home. I turn to leave—

A dark-scaled head stares back at me, silver eyes the size of a kite shield reflecting my torchlight. My hobgoblin guide relaxes in the face of the massive beast, and they call out to Geojibom by name. Her smile curls as they introduce me to her. She is kind in the way stone is: hard and still because it is her nature to be, but steady. Reliable, perhaps? When she hears I’m delving past Sekamina of my own volition, she asks a favor of me. It’s nothing more than a simple chore: one of her dear pixiu seems to have gone missing, and she offers me a way to truly traverse the Darklands as a reward. Something that will make my long journey in the dark beneath worth all this trouble.

–Diary of Yoon

She may take a more direct interest in their quest if their antagonist is someone who has stolen from her, violated an agreement with her, or directly opposed her in the past. In the event of an enemy whose goals threaten her territory, she may provide aid without requesting payment.

Moderate favors for Geojibom include sending her tips about where treasure might be, paying her with treasure she requested, and assisting her pixius if they encounter one on a mission.

Major favors would be gifting her treasures that she desires unprompted—for example, unique artwork and creative magical items worth at least 5,000 gp—or defeating someone with whom she is in conflict.

Geojibom's Gifts

Geojibom may provide the following items to adventurers working for her, but she rarely wanders far from her hoard, and prefers to send constructs, pixius, or other magical creatures to deliver rewards on her behalf. Pixius make for poor couriers, since they tend to eat treasures, but they are reliable messengers. She may also summon and send fire elementals with fireproof packages, though such entities often draw too much attention when wandering the gloam of the Darklands.

Biaoshi Rangers.name: Biaoshi Rangers
Biaoshi Rangers.text:
Throughout the Successor States the gentry are well- noted for their unquenchable thirst for luxuries from distant vistas. Such treasures are valued not only for their quality and usefulness, but also for their rarity and exclusivity. For instance, the oracular officials of Po Li compete with one another to see who among them can best decorate their robes with the colorful feathers of birds from Nagajor or the Valashmai Jungle. Petty recanters in Quain focus on collecting “cultivation materials” from across Tian Xia, as if to posture about the everpresent temptation they abstain from indulging in. Even in Lingshen, officers well known for a stern and joyless reputation, display their professional prowess by affording horses and mastiffs from the Hongal plains.

It is the acquisition of these goods which ensures careers and alliances are made and broken, and this complex system of import logistics is carried primarily on the backs of wily appraisers who traffic these goods across land and sea. Without the cunning of biaoshi rangers, this vast system of imperial desires and international acquisitions falls apart. It is they who obtain the gifts exchanged between patron and client, who follow the clues of scrutinizing merchants, and who ensure a network of luxuries and alliances remains afloat. Biaoshi rangers defend themselves against bandits and beasts, or to endure harsh environments; it is only those with a sharp eye for detail and a clear mind capable of composed professionalism who can make a career of it. A successful biaoshi ranger knows their life and livelihood is bound to a convoy and to the luxuries they must acquire and safeguard. Only those capable of defending their cargo, identifying opportunities and making quick deals have any chance of making it in the field, and even then they can rarely make it alone.

Experienced biaoshi rangers often form security bureaus, which act as offices where they can be hired as bodyguards, guides, or logisticians. These bureaus also function as training grounds for apprentices of proven merit or who can afford the often steep tuition fees. While some convoyers may be disgraced officers or former nobles seeking fortune in the borderlands, many more come from humble backgrounds where their capacities were proven through toil. Like many other industries, it is the poor who are most often tasked to take on such dangerous and thankless work for the pleasure of their societal betters. The most cunning biaoshi rangers are conscripts or veterans, shaped by Tian Xia’s many, often pointless, wars. They combine ruthless military pragmatism with street-smart strategies from the jianghu, the world of martial arts and crime. A successful biaoshi bureau aims to build a strong reputation, such that they might enrich themselves by acquiring and transporting goods for the wealthiest people across Tian Xia—albeit rarely in comfort.
